title: SAA-C03 Whitepapers and AWS Services to Master
content: 4 min readAug 27, 2023--When preparing for the SAA-C03 AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate exam, it’s crucial to focus on specific whitepapers and AWS services. Here’s a breakdown of what you should prioritize:Press enter or click to view image in full sizePhoto by Glenn Carstens-Peters on UnsplashWhitepapersAWS Well-Architected Framework Understand the principles and best practices for designing and maintaining well-architected AWS environments.An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework Learn about the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework and how it can guide your organization’s cloud journey.Cost Optimization Pillar — AWS Well-Architected Framework Dive into cost optimization strategies within the Well-Architected Framework to maximize your AWS investments.Disaster Recovery of On-Premises Applications to AWS Explore disaster recovery strategies for migrating on-premises applications to AWS for enhanced resilience.Security Best Practices for Manufacturing OT Discover security best practices tailored to the unique challenges of manufacturing environments.Core AWS Services to Focus OnEC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) Master the fundamental compute service offered by AWS, covering everything from instance types to security groups.Lambda Understand how to use Lambda for building serverless applications and integrating it with other AWS services.Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) Explore the different ELB types and their features for creating highly available systems.Auto Scaling Learn which AWS services can be auto-scaled, the triggers for scaling, and how auto scaling adjusts instance counts.Elastic Block Store (EBS) As EC2’s primary storage solution, study the types of EBS volumes, their security, backup, and restoration processes.S3 / Glacier Gain a deep understanding of Amazon S3, its storage types, and capabilities such as hosting static websites, securing access, and lifecycle policies.Storage Gateway Differentiate between Storage Gateway and other storage services like S3 or EBS, understanding their use cases and differences.EFS (Elastic File System) Know when to use EFS compared to S3, EBS, or instance store, considering cost and efficiency trade-offs.RDS / Aurora Distinguish between different RDS database engines and how they differ from Aurora. Learn about parameter groups, option groups, and subnet groups.DynamoDB Prepare for questions on DynamoDB, comparing it to RDS, Elasticache, and Redshift. Understand its importance for serverless applications.Elasticache Familiarize yourself with Elasticache Redis and its functions, especially caching mechanisms for improving data throughput.VPC/NACL/Security Groups Study all services used to create a VPC, and differentiate between network access control lists (NACLs) and security groups.Route 53 Explore Route 53’s record types, routing policies, hosted zones, and domains.IAM (Identity and Access Management) Understand IAM’s core components — users, groups, policies, and roles — and its role in securing AWS applications.CloudWatch Learn about AWS monitoring, the types of metrics sent to CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, Alarms, and custom metrics with CloudWatch Agent.CloudTrail Familiarize yourself with CloudTrail’s function and the types of logs it stores compared to CloudWatch Logs.Kinesis Gain a high-level understanding of Kinesis sharding and Kinesis Data Streams.CloudFront Study how CloudFront accelerates websites and the content sources it can serve from.SQS (Simple Queue Service) Learn why SQS is vital for decoupling systems and understand its different queue types.SNS (Simple Notification Service) Explore SNS functions and the services it can integrate with, along with supported recipients.SWF / CloudFormation / OpsWorks Differentiate the capabilities and use cases of SWF, CloudFormation, and OpsWorks.Other AWS Services to PrepareAWS Global AcceleratorElastic Fabric Adapter (EFA)Elastic Network Adapter (ENA)AWS ParallelClusterAmazon FSxAWS DataSyncAWS Directory ServiceHigh-Performance ComputingAurora ServerlessAmazon RedshiftAWS Glue and more..Additional Knowledge for the ExamAWS DataSync vs Storage GatewayUnderstand when to use AWS DataSync or Storage Gateway for efficient data transfer and storage.FSx (Cold and Hot Storage)Differentiate between FSx cold and hot storage based on data access patterns and cost considerations.Cross-Region Read Replicas vs Multi-Az RDSDecide between Cross-Region Read Replicas and Multi-AZ RDS for high availability based on your application’s needs and data redundancy.Amazon Object Key vs Object MetadataKnow when to use Amazon S3 object keys or object metadata for effective object management.Direct Connect vs Site-to-Site VPNUnderstand when to choose AWS Direct Connect or Site-to-Site VPN for secure and low-latency AWS access.AWS Config vs AWS CloudTrailDifferentiate AWS Config and AWS CloudTrail for monitoring and auditing your AWS environment.Security Group vs NACL (Network Access Control List)Determine when to use AWS security groups or NACLs to control inbound and outbound traffic.NAT Gateway vs NAT InstanceUnderstand the differences between NAT gateways and NAT instances for outbound traffic management from private subnets.Geolocation Routing Policy vs Geoproximity Routing Policy on Route 53Learn how to select routing policies in Amazon Route 53 based on traffic routing needs, such as directing users to the nearest AWS resources or global traffic distribution.This additional knowledge will be valuable for your AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C03) exam preparations. Remember to consult AWS documentation, FAQs, and utilize resources you like for comprehensive coverage. Hands-on experience with these services through lab exercises is also highly beneficial for retaining knowledge.Note: The provided content represents the minimum requirements for understanding these AWS concepts.
